incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has discovered that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provided. In one video, the fake Leal promises US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal first learned of the scheme when potential clients began calling his office last October, though the problem has dramatically worsened in recent months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an online anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically start with a social media video directing viewers to contact a phone number via WhatsApp, leading to fraudulent contracts and payment requests through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal is urging immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and avoid making immediate payments. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article recently circulated featuring Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler about an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform called Boulder Sparhaven. The interview never actually happened. This type of scam, which uses artificial intelligence to create convincing deepfake content featuring well-known Australians, is rapidly increasing. The corporate regulator ASIC removed 19,400 scams last year, a 182 percent increase, with fake investment platforms rising 151 percent and phishing scams jumping 279 percent.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is the most commonly impersonated public figure, followed by other politicians and prominent financial figures including Alan Kohler, Tom Piotrowski, and billionaires Dick Smith and Gina Rinehart. Scammers create elaborate webs of deception using fake news articles, positive reviews, and advertisements to build credibility before targeting consumers. ASIC advises people to verify Australian Financial Services licenses through their free public register and check that website information matches official records before investing. Alan Kohler has called for heavy fines against platforms hosting this content and the AI models that generate it.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A proposed class-action lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco accuses Oura, a smart ring company valued at approximately 11 billion dollars, of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit alleges that Oura's rings, which cost 300 dollars and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as claimed. According to the lawsuit, the company's algorithms and sensors lack the ability to detect the physiological signals necessary for precise sleep stage measurement, instead relying on artificial intelligence estimates that are no more reliable than a coin flip. The lawsuit highlights that Oura markets claims such as 95 percent sleep staging accuracy compared to clinical sleep labs, which use complex methods including multiple electrodes to measure brain activity.

Oura responded by defending its science and accuracy claims, stating that its rings use multiple physiological signals including heart rate, movement, and temperature to estimate sleep stages, with validation from peer-reviewed studies. The company emphasized that while Oura Ring is not a medical device or substitute for clinical sleep studies, its sleep staging has been validated favorably against the gold standard polysomnography method. It remains unclear at this early stage what compensation eligible buyers might receive if the case proceeds or settles. This marks a second legal action against Oura, following an ongoing class-action lawsuit alleging the company collected sensitive personal information without customer consent.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments and is operating a data leak site. The group used Cursor Agent, which runs Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten organizations between April and May 2026. The ESXi ransomware encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. Aurora operators also deployed custom tools like esxi_finder.py to scan networks for VMware infrastructure.

Researchers identified a second cluster of Aurora activity with medium confidence, affecting eight victim organizations across multiple countries including Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This cluster used different techniques, including SQL Server exploitation and DCSync attacks for lateral movement and data exfiltration to self-hosted S3 storage. Gambit Security provided indicators of compromise including IP addresses, domains, and file hashes to help organizations identify and defend against Aurora ransomware operations.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit alleging that Pizza Hut's new AI-powered delivery system, called Dragontail, caused significant operational problems and over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates roughly 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, claims the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together instead of delivering immediately. This resulted in cold pizzas, late deliveries, and poor customer satisfaction. Before the 2024 rollout, Chaac maintained over 90 percent on-time delivery rates and double-digit sales growth, but afterward experienced sharp declines, including a swing from positive 10 percent sales growth to negative 9 percent in New York City.

Chaac alleges Pizza Hut forced adoption of the system without adequate training or support and refused to modify it despite worsening performance metrics. The company claims Pizza Hut violated their franchise agreement by mandating continued use while failing to exercise reasonable business judgment. Pizza Hut declined to comment beyond stating it would respond through legal channels. The lawsuit comes as Pizza Hut's parent company, Yum! Brands, explores strategic options for the struggling chain and plans to close 250 US locations in the first half of the year.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other NPR staff members to defraud people seeking interviews on the popular radio show "Fresh Air." Authors, entertainers, and public figures have received highly personalized emails claiming to offer interview opportunities, complete with detailed references to their work and seemingly legitimate booking procedures. The scam eventually requests payment, typically $250 for production costs. A history professor at Misericordia University fell for the initial pitch but became suspicious when the email supposedly came directly from Gross herself and contained language that seemed AI-generated. She confirmed her suspicions when asked to pay money.

Cybersecurity experts note that artificial intelligence has made impersonation scams cheaper and more convincing than traditional versions. Red flags include requests for payment, emails from unofficial addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com, and a major radio host personally handling logistics. WHYY, NPR, and "Fresh Air" have stated they never charge guests for interviews and are working with law enforcement to investigate. Experts recommend verifying requests through legitimate organizational contacts rather than responding to suspicious emails, and they warn that such sophisticated AI-enabled scams targeting specific victims will likely become more common.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, funded by the Israeli government, published over half a million words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. The reports addressed contentious topics including Palestinian prisoner torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation, framing Israel's position as neutral research. The New York production company Piro Inc filed the operation as a foreign agent, and the institute appears to have no legitimate legal status, physical address, or named staff. The effort is part of a broader, tens of millions of dollar campaign routed through European advertising company Havas Media to shape how AI systems present arguments about Israel.

The campaign reflects broader Israeli frustrations with declining American public support, with recent polling showing Americans favor Palestinians more than Israelis for the first time and majorities expressing unfavorable views of Israel. Israeli officials have called the spending on public diplomacy efforts a failure. Researchers note the real concern is not website traffic but getting content into training data repositories that feed commercial AI models, where misinformation becomes difficult to fact-check since sources go uncited when chatbots regurgitate trained narratives.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno. The labels accuse both companies of illegally scraping thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their AI models and then directly reproducing sections of famous recordings in their generated music. The record labels submitted a lengthy list of scraped works spanning artists like The Beatles, Michael Jackson, Frank Sinatra, Bruce Springsteen, and many others.

As evidence, the record labels demonstrated they could repeatedly recreate famous songs by entering specific prompts into the AI generators. For example, prompting "1954 rock and roll billy haley comets" produced outputs mimicking Bill Haley's style and melody, while a Mariah Carey prompt generated a near-identical clone of "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The record labels claim the companies have refused to disclose their training data and assert that such copyright infringement is fair use. Two separate lawsuits were filed, one in New York against Udio and one in Massachusetts against Suno, setting up a significant court battle over generative AI's use of copyrighted material.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has reached a settlement with AI music startup Udio, resolving a lawsuit that accused the company of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence model. Under the agreement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that only uses authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs. UMG's CEO stated the deal reflects the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technology and creating new revenue opportunities. Financial terms of the settlement were not disclosed.

The lawsuit had alleged that Udio improperly used popular songs like The Temptations' "My Girl" to train its AI system, which generates original music from text prompts. This represents Udio's first major licensing agreement with a record label. The company, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, has attracted millions of users since its launch. Additionally, UMG announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized in an Los Angeles lawsuit after using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings in court filings. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire in her Carson home left it uninhabitable. She claims delays in getting State Farm's approval for repairs prevented completion of reconstruction work, leading her family to drain savings, declare bankruptcy, and lose their home to foreclosure. Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted she used an AI tool called Irys, which she mistakenly thought performed accuracy checks, resulting in seven fake case citations across eight filings.

The incident highlights a growing problem in the legal profession, where 41 percent of law firms now use generative AI. A Paris-based database has documented nearly 1,922 legal hallucinations worldwide, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney received a record ten thousand dollar fine for including 21 fabricated quotes in a brief. The trial in Meni-Siliga's case is scheduled for October, and State Farm said it expects external counsel to meet the highest ethical standards.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic Bring Free AI Bootcamp to Denver Teens
stories.Summary:
The Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic are offering a free artificial intelligence bootcamp to high school students in Denver this fall. The program is open to ninth through twelfth graders and will run over three consecutive Saturdays on October 31, November 7, and November 14. All costs including meals, transportation, and technology will be covered for participants at no charge. Applications close on September 30.

The bootcamp provides hands-on experience with AI tools and explores real-world applications across fields like healthcare, business, sports science, and career preparation. Students will work on a capstone project guided by industry mentors. This Denver bootcamp is one of more than 35 similar programs being hosted across the United States by various companies. Mark Cuban emphasized the importance of providing AI education to underserved students to prepare them for future educational and employment opportunities.

stories.Headline: Datametrex Plans to Focus on AI, Data Centre, and Patent Licensing
stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to shut down its healthcare operations to focus on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. The gradual wind-down aims to streamline the corporate structure, reduce operating costs and regulatory requirements, and improve financial performance by redirecting resources toward core business areas.

The company will manage the transition carefully, considering operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors. Management plans to assess opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the process. The strategic shift allows Datametrex to concentrate capital and resources on artificial intelligence and data centre initiatives, which align with long-term objectives. The company indicated it would provide further updates as developments occur.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: Ghana: Ai Will Enhance, Not Replace Surveyors - Ghis President
stories.Summary:
Emmanuel K. Cobbold, president of the Ghana Institution of Surveyors, addressed members at the organization's 57th Founder's Day Anniversary Celebration in Accra. He encouraged surveyors to adopt artificial intelligence and emerging technologies rather than viewing them as threats to their profession. Cobbold emphasized that while AI can assist with measurements, data analysis, and interpretation, professional surveying still requires human judgment, local expertise, and ethical responsibility. He warned that surveyors who fail to adapt to technological changes risk becoming obsolete as the profession evolves.

The institution is working to help members upgrade their skills to meet changing technological demands while maintaining professional integrity standards. Sarah Esi Ziddah, the organization's chief executive officer, noted that surveyors have significantly contributed to Ghana's development, including providing geospatial data during a boundary dispute with Côte d'Ivoire and supporting construction of an infectious disease center. The event brought together current and former members to recognize contributions to the profession and strengthen professional connections among the organization's widely dispersed membership.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: Environmental News Network - AI Project Led by UH Aims to Protect Hawaiʻi's Coastal Freshwater
stories.Summary:
The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa is launching an artificial intelligence project to forecast threats to coastal freshwater supplies and ecosystems. Associate Professor Jonghyun Lee received a $500,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to lead the initiative, which is part of a broader three-year collaborative effort worth nearly $1 million involving the University of Texas at Austin. The project aims to develop AI applications in geoscience to better understand environmental challenges.

Rising ocean levels, intensified storms, saltwater infiltration of freshwater sources, and coastal ecosystem damage present growing dangers to communities throughout the region. These threats directly endanger drinking water availability, farming operations, infrastructure, and the economic wellbeing of millions of people who depend on coastal areas.

The program will include an AI Lab for hands-on exploration of technology capabilities, an exhibition showcasing marketing solution providers, and an awards ceremony recognizing innovative organizations. Sessions will cover topics such as content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation, and analytics.
